E032-01.notes: Full date mid-sentence needs commas after the day and after the year: 'On December 21, 1913, the New York World'. A lacks the day/year comma; C lacks the comma after the year; D has no commas at all.

E032-02.notes: Register item. A, B and D are slang; 'eagerly took up' fits the formal, informational tone.

E032-03.notes: In a neither...nor subject, the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('Wynne', singular), so 'was'. B and C are plural and also shift the tense.

E032-04.notes: The current sentence covers 1913 to 1924 and leads into 'Then, in 1924'. B is off topic and unsupported. C is too general. D jumps to the present day.

E032-05.notes: Only B gives concrete sales detail (sold out its first printing, reprinted repeatedly). This is historically accurate for the 1924 Simon & Schuster Cross Word Puzzle Book.

flags: minor: some style guides still accept '1920's'; ACT treats '1920s' as the standard, so the key holds
E032-06.notes: A plural decade with no possession takes no apostrophe: '1920s'. B and D add a possessive apostrophe that has no function here.

E032-07.notes: 'People' is already plural, so the possessive is 'people's'. 'peoples'' would mean belonging to several peoples (nations); B has no possessive; C is malformed.

E032-08.notes: A writer implies and a reader infers, so editorials 'implied'. B, a participle, breaks the relative clause. D has the wrong meaning.

E032-09.notes: The sentence contrasts with the critics' mockery in the previous paragraph, so 'Still' fits. B intensifies, C signals similarity and D signals consequence; all three are illogical here.

flags: minor: the passage ends with an empty '[]' marker, a harmless artifact of the packet
E032-10.notes: 'In wartime' and 'the paper's editors' refer to sentence 2 (the Times began a crossword in 1942). Placed after sentence 2, 'the paper' clearly means the Times. Placed after sentence 3, it would split the Farrar sentence from its context. Facts are accurate: the Times began its crossword in February 1942, reportedly as a wartime diversion.
